anatomy: White blood cells can fall, raising the risk of infection. Anaemia can cause tiredness or breathlessness; low platelets can cause bruising or bleeding. Blood tests guide delays and dose changes. Fever, shaking chills or feeling suddenly unwell need the oncology emergency contact immediately.

The bowel can slow down and nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea or sore mouth can occur. Use the prescribed bowel and anti-sickness plan. Severe abdominal pain, swelling, repeated vomiting or inability to pass stool/gas needs urgent assessment for ileus; do not simply take extra laxatives.
Nerve effects may change sensation, grip, walking or bowel movement. Report changes early because the next dose may need to wait or be reduced.
Tiredness, hair thinning/loss and liver-test changes can occur. Pace activities and tell the team if eating, drinking or daily tasks become difficult.
New chest pain, sudden or worsening breathlessness, or severe allergic symptoms need urgent medical help. Previous heart disease and interacting medicines need review before treatment.
Tell staff immediately about burning, pain, swelling or leakage.

Return them to pharmacy; immediately wash any contact with contents using water or saline. Missed/late dose: contact the team for the next date. Do not double or move the weekly schedule yourself. This is pragmatic medication-safety advice, not an extra NCCP catch-up schedule.

questions.q: How do I store the capsules?
questions.a: Current Vinorelbine Accord SmPC: refrigerator 2–8°C. Confirm the dispensed brand/pack instructions; keep in original packaging and out of children’s reach. Return unused or damaged capsules to pharmacy; follow cytotoxic handling advice.

questions.q: Does dose four always use more capsules?
questions.a: No. The team reviews the lowest counts and side effects after the first three doses. Take only the current prescribed dose; severe or repeated low counts can prevent an increase.

evidence.title: Why this treatment may be chosen
evidence.intro: Studies support vinorelbine as an option in selected people with advanced non-small-cell lung cancer. The strength and type of evidence differ for the IV and capsule schedules.
evidence.population: Non-small-cell lung cancer; the cited study enrolled older adults with advanced disease.
evidence.interpretation: The team considers tumour tests, previous treatment, health, symptoms and your preferences. Results from a group cannot predict your own benefit.
evidence.limitations: Historical studies do not establish superiority over current biomarker-directed or immunotherapy options. Oral and IV study results are not interchangeable.

items.text: Discuss the disease-control aim, likely benefit and uncertainty, other lung-cancer treatments or symptom-focused care, and the burden of visits and tests. anatomy: White blood cells can fall, raising the risk of infection. Anaemia can cause tiredness or breathlessness; low platelets can cause bruising or bleeding. patient.schedule_summary: Bevacizumab 15 mg/kg is infused on Day 1 every 21 days. With platinum chemotherapy, the combined phase lasts up to six cycles, then bevacizumab may continue alone. With erlotinib, the combination continues while helpful and tolerated. Progression or unacceptable toxicity can stop either plan earlier; no fixed overall lung-treatment duration is promised.
patient.purpose: Bevacizumab blocks VEGF, a signal that supports blood-vessel growth. In selected non-squamous lung cancers it is added to another treatment to help control cancer; the balance of benefit and risk depends on the partner and tumour features.
patient.indication_text: NCCP 00215f: first-line unresectable advanced, recurrent or metastatic non-squamous NSCLC with platinum-based chemotherapy. NCCP 00215g: the corresponding first-line EGFR-activating-mutation setting with erlotinib. This is the bevacizumab component; every partner needs its own prescription, assessment and consent.
patient.administration_text: The usual bevacizumab reference dose is 15 mg/kg intravenously every 21 days. The first infusion is over 90 minutes; if tolerated, the second can be over 60 minutes and later infusions over 30 minutes. The team checks the actual prescription, blood pressure, urine and other tests before treatment.
patient.monitoring_summary: Before starting: blood count, kidney and liver tests, urine protein, blood pressure and a heart history/examination. evidence.title: Evidence depends on the treatment partner
evidence.intro: Studies have tested bevacizumab with platinum chemotherapy and, separately, with erlotinib in cancers with certain EGFR mutations. The results answer different questions.

questions.q: Which lung pathway am I following?
questions.a: Ask whether you are receiving bevacizumab with platinum chemotherapy or with erlotinib for an EGFR-mutated cancer. Their partner schedules, checks and phase changes differ.

The platinum combination is given for up to six cycles, after which bevacizumab can continue alone if appropriate. The erlotinib pathway has no automatic six-cycle switch. The team reviews benefit, side effects and your priorities.

questions.q: What happens if urine protein or blood pressure rises?
questions.a: The team may repeat tests, treat blood pressure or pause bevacizumab. Severe problems may mean stopping it. Do not restart after a pause without an agreed plan.

questions.q: What if I need an operation or dental work?
questions.a: Tell the oncology team before the procedure. Bevacizumab can slow healing, and the team must coordinate any treatment break and check healing before restarting.

evidence.trial: ECOG 4599 and JO25567, kept as separate treatment contexts
evidence.population: ECOG 4599: 878 selected patients with recurrent/advanced non-squamous NSCLC, ECOG 0–1; significant haemoptysis, brain metastases and squamous histology excluded. JO25567: Japanese chemotherapy-naive EGFR-mutated stage IIIB/IV or postoperative recurrent non-squamous NSCLC; 152 treated patients.
evidence.comparison: ECOG 4599: carboplatin/paclitaxel ± bevacizumab 15 mg/kg every three weeks. JO25567: daily erlotinib ± bevacizumab 15 mg/kg every three weeks.
evidence.applicability: Both test the 15 mg/kg every-21-day component but with different complete combinations and populations. Neither establishes bevacizumab monotherapy as initial lung treatment.
